pr_title: Enhance embed URL handling and validation system

validations.droid_claim:
[P1] Disqus import reply posts may be cooked incorrectly

The Disqus import now seeds the topic via `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (raw HTML path), but follow-up posts created in the loop still pass Disqus HTML in `raw` without setting `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. Since `PostCreator` ignores a `cooked` opt, this HTML will be run through the normal cooking pipeline and may be mangled. Set `cook_method` (or convert to Markdown) for consistency with the imported OP.
validations.impact: Disqus reply posts will have their HTML mangled by Discourse's normal cooking pipeline, producing incorrectly formatted content in imported threads.
validations.reasoning: Verified in PostCreator#setup_post (lib/post_creator.rb:208-216). The `cooked` attribute is NOT in the list of opts passed through to the post instance (line 213-214 only passes :post_type, :no_bump, :cooking_options, :image_sizes, :acting_user, :invalidate_oneboxes). So even though the Disqus import passes `cooked: p[:cooked]` in attrs, PostCreator ignores it. Then at line 105, `post.cooked ||= post.cook(post.raw, cooking_options)` re-cooks the raw HTML through the normal pipeline. The OP is correctly imported via TopicEmbed.import which sets `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, but reply posts don't get this treatment.
validations.code_evidence:
disqus.thor lines 139-148 pass `raw: p[:cooked], cooked: p[:cooked]` but no cook_method.
PostCreator#setup_post (post_creator.rb:208) creates post with only `raw: @opts[:raw]`.
Line 213-214: `[:post_type, :no_bump, :cooking_options, :image_sizes, :acting_user, :invalidate_oneboxes].each` — :cooked not included.
Line 105: `post.cooked ||= post.cook(post.raw, cooking_options)` — will always re-cook since cooked is nil.

validations.droid_claim:
[P0] SSRF risk: open-uri follows redirects in import_remote

`Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)` will follow HTTP redirects by default. Even if the initial `@embed_url` host is validated elsewhere, a 30x redirect can send the fetch to internal IPs/metadata endpoints, enabling SSRF. Validate the final URL after redirects and/or disable/limit redirects and disallow private/loopback address ranges.
validations.impact: An attacker who controls an embed URL can use HTTP redirects to make the Discourse server fetch internal resources (cloud metadata endpoints, internal services), leaking sensitive data like cloud credentials.
validations.reasoning: Verified in topic_embed.rb line 48: `open(url).read` uses Ruby's Kernel#open (with open-uri loaded from other requires in the app). open-uri follows HTTP redirects by default with no restrictions on target IP ranges. There is no validation of the final resolved URL. The url comes from user-controlled sources: RSS feed links (poll_feed.rb) and Disqus thread links (disqus.thor). No SSRF protection middleware or URL validation was found in the codebase for this path.
validations.code_evidence:
topic_embed.rb:48: `doc = Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)`
open-uri is loaded in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:7 and multiple other files.
No URL validation or redirect restrictions found in TopicEmbed or its callers.

validations.droid_claim:
[P0] JavaScript injection via unescaped request.referer

`request.referer` is interpolated into a JS string literal in `parent.postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>')` without JS escaping, so a crafted Referer header containing quotes/`</script>` can break out and execute script in the embed frame. Use `j(request.referer)`/`escape_javascript` (or avoid embedding it directly) to prevent XSS.
validations.impact: An attacker can craft a Referer header containing JavaScript code that executes in the embed frame, potentially stealing session data or performing actions on behalf of the user viewing the embedded content.
validations.reasoning: Verified in embed.html.erb line 11: `parent.postMessage({type: 'discourse-resize', height: document['body'].offsetHeight}, '<%= request.referer %>');`. ERB's `<%= %>` HTML-escapes the output (converting < > " & to entities), but it does NOT JavaScript-escape it. A referer containing a single quote `'` breaks out of the JS string literal. While `</script>` would be HTML-escaped to `</script>`, a single quote in the referer (which is valid in URLs) would terminate the string and allow arbitrary JS injection. The `j()` or `escape_javascript` helper is needed here.
validations.code_evidence:
embed.html.erb:11: `parent.postMessage({type: 'discourse-resize', height: document['body'].offsetHeight}, '<%= request.referer %>');`
No escape_javascript or j() helper used. A referer like `http://evil.com/page?x='%2balert(1)%2b'` would break out of the string.

validations.droid_claim:
[P1] Possible NoMethodError when feed item lacks content

`i.content.scrub` assumes every RSS/Atom item has `content`; many feeds only provide `description`/`summary`. When `i.content` is nil this will raise and stop the polling job. Coerce to string and/or fall back to other fields before calling `scrub`.
validations.impact: Any RSS feed that uses `description` instead of `content` (which is common in RSS 2.0 feeds) will crash the PollFeed scheduled job with NoMethodError, preventing all feed polling from working.
validations.reasoning: Verified in poll_feed.rb line 35: `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. SimpleRSS returns nil for `i.content` when the feed item only has a `description` or `summary` element (which is the standard for RSS 2.0 feeds). Calling `.scrub` on nil raises NoMethodError. The job has `sidekiq_options retry: false` (line 13), so it won't retry and feed polling will be broken until the next scheduled run, which will fail again.
validations.code_evidence:
poll_feed.rb:35: `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`
poll_feed.rb:13: `sidekiq_options retry: false`
SimpleRSS gem returns nil for missing elements. RSS 2.0 spec uses `description`, not `content`.
